observation: Two original party sprite decodes reproduce all 163483 output bytes, including the captured adjacent source-memory inputs. Seventeen directory changes and 43 source-index observations correlate exactly. The qualified physics window compares 61 source-header gravity prefixes, six sprite-A1 impulses and 126 vertical stages: 63 airborne and 63 floor outcomes. All 53 corrupted traces are rejected, and both captures preserve all 66 artifacts from the independently built uninstrumented control.
interpretation: The original jump impulse is supplied by sprite animation command A1, in a namespace separate from field-event bytecode. Observed headers supply gravity, and the bounded field stage integrates old velocity before acceleration and floor handling. Full animation, walking/running, floor selection and later collision/ceiling/layer response remain unreconstructed. This exact subset does not close player readiness or timing proof.
author: Codex /root, independent original-source and execution analysis on 2026-09-08

preconditions: Use the exact selected original Disc 1, the pinned Nix shells and fresh private capture/report paths.
The existing field23 control route uses the previously qualified field adapter and ordinary inputs; no new setup writes are added.
The loader entry hook follows the MIPS argument-load delay. Observe adjacent source bytes rather than substituting disc padding.
commands: Run the same scenario command twice, adding --trace-instructions <loader-spec> or <physics-spec> and distinct fresh output directories.
env PYTHONPATH=. python .local/analysis/phase1-field-motion-20260908/audit-jump-v2.py <fresh-version> (set capture paths when using new runs)
validation.expected: Exact original source, state, full output bytes, source boundaries and call correlations. Reject altered input/output evidence and preserve all independent control artifacts.
validation.actual: 81 loader records and 7720 physics records qualify with no guard failures, unavailable ranges, exhausted budgets or collector errors. Two complete resource decodes, 61 gravity prefixes, six impulses and 126 vertical stages compare exactly. All 53 corruptions are rejected; each capture matches all 66 uninstrumented control artifacts. Fourteen public synthetic boundary tests pass.
validation.tolerance: Exact integer arithmetic and complete captured-byte/hash equality with original pointer storage, overlapping ranges, call order and return/stack checks. Other animation-command effects remain explicitly opaque. No output masks, universal cadence inference or hardware exception emulation.

unobserved_source_branches: Nonzero impulse velocity reference, reference-disabled path and differing operand/scale/rate/divisor values.
Different signed gravity coefficients, zero divisors and hardware exception behavior.
Terrain-disabled or different-attribute lookups, vertical-stage layer changes and terrain marker retention.
Negative animation modes and remaining sprite commands, resource/component formats and complete animation state changes.
limitations: The two resources and this original route do not establish complete sprite formats, resource lifetime, all decoder callers or other profiles.
All 61 enclosing animation calls are correlated; 7074 other sprite-command returns are counted as opaque and are not claimed reconstructed.
The selected floor is an input. Complete walking/running, collision, layer, ceiling, rollback, history/follower and camera behavior remain required.
The source header/impulse values and observed every-second-frontend vertical updates do not establish universal game cadence or hardware timing.
Independent review, 15 broad Phase 1 todos and nine slice proof domains remain open. Native gameplay is unimplemented.
